caption: Average Change in INC score from combined layer to base layer, where a negative score means the base layer was better than the combined one and vice versa. The gray and orange bars indicate whether the input to the compression layer is inferred frames or lexical signal, respectively. In all cases, inferred frames has a better effect on base layer and lexical signal has improved combined layer's performance.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the average change in INC score resulting from combining layers, comparing the effects of using inferred frames versus lexical signal. The horizontal axis, labeled “Observation Probability,” displays values ranging from 0.2 to 0.9 with a linear scale, and the vertical axis, labeled “Average Change Compression Probability,” spans from -3 to 2, with tick marks indicating intervals of 0.5. The gray bars represent inferred frames, with a minimum value of approximately -3.2 and a maximum value of -0.6, and the orange bars represent lexical signal, exhibiting a minimum value of approximately -0.8 and a maximum value of 0.9.  The bars are ordered from left to right according to the ‘Observation Probability’ values, and there is no visual emphasis applied to the bars.
